name: Full screen intent
plain: Lets a notification take over the screen like an incoming call or alarm.
meaning: Interrupts the user with a full-screen UI. Limited to calling and alarm apps on Android 14 and later.

android.prompt_ui: Settings toggle: Manage full screen intents
android.revocation: Settings > Special app access > Full screen intents
android.store_policy: Play: declaration required from May 31, 2024; only calling and alarm apps by default from Jan 22, 2025 on apps targeting 14+
android.note: Android 14 limits default grant to calling and alarm apps.

ios.note: iOS has no full-screen takeover; CallKit shows incoming calls.

limits.headline: Can take over your Android screen for a call or alarm, only if you allow it
limits.user_action: A call comes in, or an alarm goes off, while your phone is locked
can: Open a full screen alert for an incoming call or alarm
Show it even when the phone is locked
Do this by default if it is a calling or alarm app
cannot: Do this for other apps on Android 14 or newer unless you turn on Manage full screen intents
Take over your screen on iPhone, which has no full screen takeover
Skip your choice if you switch the toggle off
limits.reach_label: Only calls and alarms, unless you allow
limits.differs: Android 14 limits this to calling and alarm apps by default. iPhone shows incoming calls through CallKit, never a takeover.

story.what_it_is: Lets a notification take over the whole screen, like a ringing call or alarm.

marketing.name: Full screen intent limits
marketing.pitch: Google restricts full screen alerts to calling and alarm apps starting with Android 14.

story.for_you: Your phone rings with a big call screen even when locked. For other apps, you must turn it on in settings.
story.for_makers: Makers of calling and alarm apps need it to cut through. Google limited it because ads and promotions used it to interrupt people.

use_cases.example: A video call app fills the screen when someone rings.
An alarm clock app takes over the lock screen at wake time.
A driver app shows a big ride request screen.
A fall alert app shows a full screen check in.
A doorbell app opens a live camera when someone rings.
Past ad apps tried this for takeover ads, which Google now blocks.
A dispatch app shows an urgent job screen to a driver.

story.android_note: Android 14 grants it by default only to calling and alarm apps. You can switch it in settings.
story.ios_note: iOS has no takeover. CallKit shows incoming calls.

technical_bounds: iOS has no general full screen takeover

linkedin.how: USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is declared in Android build 4.1.995 (Exodus snippet). LinkedIn has no consumer calling feature seen; may be library residue. Unverified.

history.change: Aug 26, 2026: geofencing no longer an approved foreground service use
Jan 22, 2025: only calling and alarm apps granted by default
Limited to calling and alarm apps by default
Full-screen intents limited to apps whose core function is calls or alarms; grant revocable
USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT introduced as a normal permission
